name: UPS
boundary: Historical diesel well-to-wheels versus electricity-generation-and-use benchmark; vehicle and battery manufacture excluded; no UPS total
technology: Battery-electric delivery trucks and depot charging
summary: Electric delivery vehicles already operate at UPS. An independent delivery-fleet study quantifies operating emissions savings under a specified grid and duty cycle; UPS’s remaining eligible routes are unknown.
opportunity: Identify still-diesel routes with suitable payload, range and depot power, then assess vehicle and charging finance.
constraints: The study concerns Frito-Lay Class 6 delivery trucks, not measured UPS vehicles. Match duty cycle and service before transfer.
Historical local-grid performance is not a universal reduction. Recalculate for present vehicle efficiency and electricity supply.
Calculation includes generation, transmission and charging losses and diesel well-to-wheels emissions; vehicle and battery production and disposal are excluded.
Eligible unconverted activity is unknown. Do not multiply this factor by company diesel or Scope 1 totals.
Existing routing and electric deployments are achieved improvements. Additionality and debt repayment remain unverified.
Main GRI inventory says 14.898 Mt while segment totals show 14.897 Mt; the 0.001 Mt discrepancy is unresolved.
sources: Technology · NREL field evaluation, printed pp. 7–8, 14, 20–21
Existing deployment and routing · UPS 2025 overview
Commercial deployment · UPS IVECO eDaily, June 2024
steps: Separate company direct inventory from the delivery intervention.
NREL reports 1,414.93 diesel versus 759.06 electric gCO₂e/mile under its historical local-electricity assumptions.
Normalize their difference to 1,000 matched operating tonnes: about 464 tonnes avoided.
Obtain UPS route, fuel, power, payload, replacement and charging data before scaling; account for manufacturing and financing additionality.
